caseAssertions.observation: Protections now execute inside subscribe before the separate tracking batch. A real subscribe call whose protection decision returns blocked exits normally; the adapter then still applies either ALLOW or DENY. Both operations were separately exercised. A raised subscribe failure instead prevents tracking. The old denial-first ordering is obsolete, but the protection-return result does not gate tracking writes.

caseAssertions.scope: Local MySQL permission persistence through real consumer and permission service. Workflow exception injected at execute boundary; Sentry/consumer/retry metrics captured.
caseAssertions.observation: Real permission-service fault probes confirmed both terminal and exhausted-retryable DENY failures leave the prior stored ALLOW unchanged. Sentry capture fires, but neither consumer StatsD nor retry StatsD increments and no consumer retry is requested. The expected distinguishable consumer error counter therefore does not cover these failed revocations. The no-email drop counter is separately verified by the consumer tests.
